Subject: FintechCo  Logging/redaction follow-up & next steps

Thanks again for the time today  great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to capture the follow-ups and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the security and logging requirements.

Recap (high level):
- FintechCo needs request/response logging for troubleshooting and audit, but all PII must be redacted before logs are stored.
- Retention target: ~90 days (FintechOps asks for 90d for initial retention).
- Data residency: US-only for production traces; development logs can be multi-region.
- Specific ask: clarify handling of headers and trace IDs (preserve trace IDs for correlation, but they must not be directly linkable to PII).

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
1) Share a short logging/redaction spec (attached) that outlines our options: ingestion-time regex masking, model-assisted PII detection, token-level masking, and sampling controls.
2) Provide our SOC2 summary (attached) and a short matrix of artifacts we can share for procurement.
3) Confirm whether hashed/irreversible trace IDs are acceptable for correlation.
4) Schedule a 30-min technical follow-up next week with FintechCo SRE/security + our infra/security engineers.

Please confirm the PII categories you want redacted (examples below) and whether 90 days retention and US residency meet your procurement bar. If there are any legal requirements beyond SOC2 (e.g., additional questionnaires), loop Legal and we can prioritize.

Examples of PII we discussed (please confirm): names, account numbers, payment instrument identifiers, SSNs, tokens/keys, full card numbers.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, logging-redaction-specs.xlsx

Thanks,

Hi Marissa  thanks for the write-up and for the materials on the call. Quick responses inline: 

- PII categories: confirmed  names, account numbers, payment instrument identifiers, SSNs, tokens/keys, full PANs. Also want to include device identifiers where they can be linked to a person.
- Retention: 90 days is our baseline for logs used in investigations; we'll need an option to extend to 365 days for specific audit windows.
- Data residency: production logs must be stored in the US only (we're regulated). Development/staging can be in other regions if flagged.
- Trace IDs/headers: we need to preserve correlation IDs for our observability pipelines, but they must be irreversible and not usable to reconstruct PII. Will hashed trace IDs (SHA-256 with a salt) suffice? We also want the ability to strip or mask sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, x-client-secret).

A couple of clarifying questions:
1) Will Redwood logs include the full prompt/request body (i.e., user input) by default, or is that opt-in?
2) Do you support per-customer logging policies (so we can enable more aggressive redaction for regulated tenants)?

Happy to do the technical follow-up next week  Ben and I are available Tue/Wed mornings (PST).

Thanks,
Aisha
Director, Security & Compliance | FintechCo
aisha@fintechco.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: FintechCo  Logging/redaction follow-up & next steps

Hi Aisha  thanks for the quick clarifications. High-level answers and our recommended approach below (happy to dive deeper on the technical call).

1) Default logging behavior:
- By default our hosted API captures metadata (timestamps, model, latency, request size) and a configurable request/response payload sampling. We do not persist full request/response bodies to long-term logs by default for all customers; persistence of full prompts/outputs is opt-in and can be controlled per-customer.

2) PII redaction approach:
- Ingestion-time: regex-based masks for common patterns (SSN, PAN), plus model-assisted detectors to catch names, addresses, and free-text PII.
- Token-level masking: we can persist tokenized placeholders rather than raw text for sensitive fields (e.g., replace with <REDACTED-EMAIL>).
- Trace IDs: we can persist correlation IDs as irreversible hashes (SHA-256 with per-customer salt) so they remain usable for correlation but cannot be reverse-engineered.

3) Headers & trace data:
- We support configurable header allow/deny lists. By default we strip Authorization, Cookie, and any header matching x-client-* unless explicitly allowed.

4) Retention & residency:
- Retention: configurable by customer at the tenant level. Default retention for logs is 90 days; we can extend to 365 days or longer on request (and for dedicated/private deployments).
- Residency: Hosted production storage can be pinned to US-only regions; for stricter residency we offer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) where all logs and control plane can remain in-customer VPC.

Attachments: logging-redaction-specs.xlsx (contains config knobs and sample regexes), redwood-logging-controls-diagram.png.

Next steps we propose:
- Technical 30-min deep dive (SRE + Security)  Tue/Wed morning PST works for us; propose Tue 10am PST.
- We'll prepare an artifact matrix for procurement (SOC2 + list of evidence) and share before the call.

@David  can you confirm the SOC2 artifact list and whether we can share redacted examples of logs?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: FintechCo  Logging/redaction follow-up & next steps

Hi Aisha & Ben  following up from Priyom's note with security-confirmed details.

What we can commit to today (summary):
- PII redaction: supported via layered approach: pattern-based masking + NLP detection + optional manual field allowlist. We can provide redacted log samples (synthetic or scrubbed) for procurement.
- Headers: we can configure global header denylist (Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, x-client-secret, x-api-key). Any header not on the denylist can be allowed but will be documented; per-tenant overrides supported.
- Trace IDs: we will persist only hashed correlation IDs (SHA-256 + customer-specific salt) for the hosted product. For Dedicated/Private customers, we can support customer-managed salts or HSM-backed keying for irreversible hashing.
- Prompt/request bodies: storing full prompts is opt-in per-tenant. Default is no long-term persistence of raw prompt/output; if you opt in, we recommend token-level masking for any detected PII.
- Retention/residency: 90 days default, extendable to 365+; production storage can be restricted to US regions. For highest assurance, Redwood Private keeps logs under customer control.

Operational controls we offer:
- Sampling: configurable ingestion sampling and write-through policies (e.g., keep 100% of errors, sample successful requests).
- Access controls: role-based access with audit logs; ability to disable access to raw logs for support engineers without explicit approval.
- Evidence: SOC2 summary attached; we can provide an artifact matrix (control owners, evidence types, sample redacted logs) under an NDA.

Next steps:
1) Agree technical deep-dive time (we're good for Tue 10am PST).
2) I'll produce a short artifact list and a redacted-sample package for procurement (will share Drive link).
3) If FintechCo wants, we can prep a short RFC including sample regexes and a per-tenant redaction policy template.

Thanks  looking forward to the follow-up call.

David Kim
Head of Security | Redwood Inference
